replies.user: What's the club meeting about this week?
replies.raw:
The next meeting is **"Ethical Dilemmas: Decisions That Will Define the Future"** — Thursday at 8:20 AM in the MHS Library Classroom.

The big questions on the table: Who's morally responsible when an autonomous system causes harm? Should AI ever make life-or-death decisions without a human override?

Which of those questions do you find most interesting — or most unsettling?

replies.user: Which of the blog posts should I read before it?
replies.raw:
Nathan Dozois's **"Who Gets to Tell the Robot No?"** is the most directly relevant.

It covers a real case where Anthropic refused to let the Pentagon use Claude in autonomous weapons — exactly the kind of human-override question the meeting will dig into.

Want a quick preview of the argument so you know what to look for when you read it?

replies.user: What question should I bring to the meeting?
replies.raw:
What's your gut take on the Anthropic-Pentagon situation — should a private company be able to set limits on how a government uses its AI?

Start there. Your answer to that will surface the question worth bringing.
